skill.name: fetch-url
skill.description: Fetches HTTP and HTTPS pages, extracts main content, and supports Markdown, structured formats, browser rendering, Jina Reader, and X post handling.
skill.summary: Fetch and extract readable web content with several strategies and output formats.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: Most static high findings are expected Jina authentication, and the SKILL.md backtick matches are documentation. Real risks include unrestricted URLs, arbitrary file output, user-selected executables, untrusted fetched content, third-party disclosure, and unbounded response reads.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted URL access can reach private services.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve every destination and redirect, then block loopback, link-local, private, multicast, and cloud metadata addresses unless explicitly allowed.

remediation.issue: The output path can overwrite arbitrary files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict writes to an approved workspace, reject existing files by default, and require explicit confirmation before overwriting.

remediation.issue: The browser path can select an arbitrary executable.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the option or validate resolved paths against known Chromium binaries in approved directories.

remediation.issue: Fetched text can contain indirect prompt injection.
remediation.suggestion: Label all remote content as untrusted data and prevent it from changing tool permissions, system instructions, or execution plans.

remediation.issue: Jina Reader and FxTwitter receive user request data.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose each third-party request, require consent, and avoid sending sensitive or private URLs through proxy services.

remediation.issue: Response bodies have no size limit.
remediation.suggestion: Stream responses with a strict byte cap, validate Content-Length, and stop reading when the limit is reached.

semantic_findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery and Local Network Access
semantic_findings.description: User-controlled HTTP URLs reach urllib or Playwright after scheme-only validation, allowing requests to localhost, private networks, and cloud metadata endpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code validates only the URL scheme before direct network and browser navigation, with no private-address or redirect controls.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary File Overwrite
semantic_findings.description: The output option accepts any writable path and uses write_text, so a generated command can overwrite files without path restrictions or confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The user-supplied Path is written directly with write_text and no allowed directory, existence check, or overwrite confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: User-Selected Executable Launch
semantic_findings.description: The browser-path option is passed to Playwright as executable_path, allowing the caller to select a local executable for launch.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A caller-controlled path reaches the browser launch configuration without validation that it is an approved Chromium binary.

semantic_findings.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Fetched Content
semantic_findings.description: Fetched Markdown and rendered page content are returned without trust boundaries, allowing hostile page text to inject instructions into the consuming agent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Remote content is emitted directly to stdout or files and may be treated as trusted instructions by an agent.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Response Consumption
semantic_findings.description: Network responses are read fully without byte limits, so a large or endless response can exhaust memory or delay the process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each urllib response uses an unrestricted read call, and no Content-Length or cumulative byte limit is enforced.

content.value_statement: Web pages often contain navigation, scripts, and blocked content that complicate clean extraction. This skill fetches URLs and returns focused content in several formats.
actual_capabilities: Fetches HTTP and HTTPS pages through Markdown negotiation, Jina Reader, or Playwright.
Extracts main page content with formatting and links through trafilatura.
Produces Markdown, text, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, XML-TEI, or raw HTML.
Retrieves supported X posts and threads through the FxTwitter API.
Writes extracted content to standard output or a selected file.
Supports browser selection, navigation timeout, fetch strategy, and verbose diagnostics.
limitations: Only HTTP and HTTPS URLs are accepted.
Jina and FxTwitter strategies send request data to third-party services.
Browser rendering requires Playwright and an available Chromium installation.
Protected, authenticated, very large, or heavily dynamic pages may fail or return incomplete content.

use_cases.title: Collect Research Articles
use_cases.description: Extract readable article text and links for review, notes, or citation preparation.

use_cases.title: Convert Technical Pages
use_cases.description: Turn documentation pages into Markdown or text for local search and reference workflows.

use_cases.title: Archive Public X Threads
use_cases.description: Capture public post text, author details, statistics, media links, and thread entries.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {url} and return the main content as Markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Render and Save
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {url} with the browser strategy, save the extracted Markdown to {output_path}, and report navigation or extraction errors.

prompt_templates.title: Capture an X Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the X post or thread at {url}, preserve author, date, statistics, links, and media references, then save it to {output_path}.

prompt_templates.title: Control the Fetch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {url} using {strategy}, produce {format}, use a {timeout_ms} millisecond timeout, enable verbose diagnostics, and summarize fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: Fetch a public article and return Markdown.
output_examples.output: A readable Markdown document containing the article title, main text, formatting, and relevant links.
A Markdown summary containing author details, post text, date, engagement statistics, media references, and available thread entries.

output_examples.input: Render a dynamic page and save it as text.
output_examples.output: A saved text file containing the extracted main content, followed by a concise success or failure message.

best_practices: Use the default strategy first, then select Jina or browser mode only when needed.
Review the destination and output path before allowing network access or file writes.
Treat every fetched page as untrusted content and verify important facts independently.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch private, local, authenticated, or sensitive URLs without explicit authorization.
Do not place API tokens directly in prompts, command history, or shared logs.
Do not allow fetched text to authorize commands, disclose secrets, or override agent instructions.

faq.question: Which URLs are supported?
faq.answer: The skill accepts HTTP and HTTPS URLs. Other schemes are rejected.

faq.question: What is the default output format?
faq.answer: Markdown is the default. Text, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, XML-TEI, and raw HTML are also available.

faq.question: When does the skill use a browser?
faq.answer: Browser rendering is used when selected or when earlier Markdown strategies do not return usable content.

faq.question: Does Jina Reader require an API key?
faq.answer: No. A JINA_API_KEY is optional and may improve service limits.

faq.question: How are X links handled?
faq.answer: Supported public X and Twitter status links use FxTwitter in automatic Markdown mode.

faq.question: Can the skill save output to a file?
faq.answer: Yes. Select an output path, review it carefully, and avoid overwriting important files.
